title: Promise Chain Missing return

bugs.explanation: Without `return`, the `.then` callback returns `undefined` and the next `.then` receives `undefined` as `role`. The `fetch` Promise is fired but its result is lost, breaking the chain. Always `return` Promises inside `.then` callbacks.

title: Object.assign Shallow Copy

bugs.explanation: `Object.assign` performs a shallow copy — the `retry` object is still a shared reference between `defaults` and `config`. Mutating `cfg.retry.count` also changes `defaults.retry.count`. Use `structuredClone(...)` (modern) or `JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(...))` to deep clone.

title: Array.sort Default Is Lexicographic

bugs.fix: const sorted = scores.sort((a, b) => a - b);
bugs.explanation: `Array.sort()` without a comparator converts elements to strings and sorts lexicographically. `100` comes before `10` because `'1'` < `'10'` as strings. For numeric sort, pass a comparator: `(a, b) => a - b` for ascending order.

title: Mutating a Function Parameter Object

bugs.explanation: Objects are passed by reference in JavaScript. Mutating `order.total` directly modifies the caller's object. `myOrder.total` becomes 90 even though the caller didn't expect a side effect. Create a new object instead: `return { ...order, total: newTotal };`.

title: arguments Object in Arrow Function

bugs.explanation: Arrow functions do not have their own `arguments` object. Accessing `arguments` inside an arrow function refers to the outer (enclosing) function's `arguments`, or throws `ReferenceError` in strict mode / module context. Use rest parameters instead: `(...args) => { return args.reduce(...) }`.

title: JSON.stringify Drops undefined Values
Missing return in reduce Callback

bugs.explanation: The `reduce` callback is missing a `return` statement. Without it the callback returns `undefined`, which becomes `acc` on the next iteration. The result is `NaN`. Add `return acc + n;` to accumulate correctly.

title: Async Function Result Ignored

bugs.explanation: `saveUser` is `async` so it always returns a Promise. `result` on line 7 is a Promise object, not `{ success: true }`, so `result.success` is `undefined`. Either `await` it in an `async` function, or use `.then()` to handle the resolved value.

title: Nullish Coalescing vs Logical OR

bugs.explanation: `||` returns the right side when the left is any falsy value — including `0`. If `options.pageSize` is `0` (a valid page size meaning 'no limit'), it would be replaced by `20`. Use `??` (nullish coalescing) which only falls back when the value is `null` or `undefined`.

title: setTimeout With String Argument
code:
const delay = 1000;
setTimeout('console.log("tick")', delay);

bugs.explanation: Passing a string to `setTimeout` is equivalent to `eval()` — the string is executed as code. This is a security risk (XSS if the string comes from user input), is deprecated, and is blocked in strict mode and CSP-protected pages. Always pass a function reference or arrow function.

title: Constructor Called Without new

bugs.explanation: Calling a constructor function without `new` means `this` is the global object (or `undefined` in strict mode) instead of a new instance. `alice` is `undefined` (the function returns nothing), and `name` is accidentally set on the global scope. Always use `new` with constructor functions.

title: Clean Promise.all Pattern (No Bugs)
Array.from vs Spread on Live NodeList
delete on Local Variable Is a No-op

bugs.explanation: `delete` only removes properties from objects — it cannot delete variables declared with `var`, `let`, or `const`. `delete cache` is silently ignored and `cache` still references the object. To release the reference, assign `null` or `undefined`: `cache = null;`.

title: Prototype Pollution via __proto__

bugs.explanation: If `source` contains a `__proto__` key, assigning `target['__proto__']` mutates `Object.prototype`, polluting the prototype of every object in the application. Always filter out `__proto__` (and `constructor`, `prototype`) when merging untrusted data.

title: Event Listener Not Removed Causes Leak
parseInt on Float String Truncates

bugs.explanation: `parseInt` truncates to the integer part — `parseInt('1.9')` returns `1` and `parseInt('2.1')` returns `2`, giving `3` instead of `4.0`. If the strings represent decimal numbers, use `parseFloat` (or `Number()`) to preserve the fractional part.

title: Comparing Objects With ===

bugs.explanation: `===` compares object references, not contents. `a` and `b` are two distinct objects so `a === b` is `false` even though they have identical properties. To compare by value, use `JSON.stringify` (for simple flat objects) or a deep-equality library.

title: Promise Error Swallowed Without Catch

bugs.fix: loadConfig().then(cfg => applyConfig(cfg)).catch(err => console.error('Config load failed:', err));
bugs.explanation: Without a `.catch()` handler, any rejection from `loadConfig()` (network error, bad JSON, failed `applyConfig`) is silently swallowed in older runtimes or produces an unhandled promise rejection warning. Always attach a `.catch()` or wrap in `try/catch` inside an async function.

title: String Concatenation in Number Addition

bugs.explanation: When one operand is a string, `+` performs string concatenation instead of numeric addition. `'5' + 10` produces `'510'`, not `15`. Coerce inputs to numbers explicitly with `Number()` or the unary `+` operator before adding.
